steps.body: Subtracting works the same way: break both numbers into hundreds, tens, ones, then subtract each spot. 486 − 253: hundreds 400−200=200, tens 80−50=30, ones 6−3=3. Combine: 233.
Take away place by place, then build what's left.

commonBuilds.feedback: That builds 739 = 486 + 253 — the minus sign asks you to take 253 AWAY, not pile it on.
Check the cubes: 6 − 3 = 3, not 4. Each place settles its own bill: 2 flats, 3 rods, 3 cubes.

widget.missFeedback: Subtract each place by itself: 4−2 flats, 8−5 rods, 6−3 cubes.
widget.successFeedback: 233 — every place paid its own bill, no trading needed. Keep that trade idea ready: the next problem's ones come up short.

predict.reveal: Every top digit covers its bill — 6 ≥ 3, 8 ≥ 5, 4 ≥ 2 — so 233 reads straight off. The next one, 342 − 127, has 2 − 7 waiting in the ones: THAT's when a rod gets traded down.

steps.body: When a spot doesn't have enough to subtract, trade DOWN — 1 ten breaks into 10 ones, or 1 hundred breaks into 10 tens, giving you enough to subtract.

commonErrors.feedback: The ones (2) aren't enough for 7 — trade 1 ten for 10 ones first: 12-7=5. Combine: 215.
That adds instead of subtracting. Combine the DIFFERENCES: 200+10+5=215.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Trade 1 ten for 10 ones: ones become 12, tens become 3. 12-7=5, 3-2=1, 3-1=2. Combine: 200+10+5=215.

steps.body: A trade-down can cascade too — if the tens spot is also short after trading, trade a hundred down into tens first.

commonErrors.feedback: The tens spot is empty (0) — trade a hundred down into tens first, then trade a ten into ones. Combine carefully: 234.
That adds instead of subtracting. The correct difference is 234.

steps.body: Subtract by spot, trading a bigger spot down into a smaller one whenever a spot doesn't have enough.
takeaways: Subtract hundreds, tens, and ones each on their own.
When a spot is too small, trade 1 of the next spot over into 10 of the smaller spot.
A trade-down can cascade through more than one spot, even across an empty spot.
